VORSA HB-10: the hacking-seconds edit

Here's footage of our dive watch, the VORSA HB-10, a 36,000 vph hi-beat. Make it an aura edit for Reels: slow-mo on the beat, a real drop, 9:16.

What the skill did

  • Rendered its own footage first: an invented chrome dive watch in three.js, nine macro shots at 120 fps with real depth of field, motion blur and grain. No people, no real brands.
  • Everything sits on one 150 BPM grid, because 36,000 vph is 10 ticks a second, the 16th-note rate. The escapement ticks are the hi-hats, and the opening counter steps from 06000 to 36000 on them.
  • The silence before the drop is the watch's hacking seconds. The crown pops and the seconds hand freezes in black and white. The drop restarts it in colour, on an inverted, lume-tinted impact frame.
  • Velocity ramps run 4x into each hit and 0.25x on it. Zoom punches land on the kicks and shake on the kicks and claps, with zoom blur, an RGB split and a light sweep. Uneven freeze-stops inside the drop are more hacks.
  • Type: the count-up, then 36000 masked over the ticking dial, then VORSA set into the lume dial as the studio lights go out. The grade is crushed and glowing, black and white until the drop.

Sound

  • A synthesised E-minor bed: arpeggio and pad over a 10 Hz tick-tock, with bezel clicks and a crown-winding ratchet in the build.
  • The hack: a riser and a sub swell stop dead on the crown's click, then 0.6 s of near silence. The drop is an 808 sliding 2.5 semitones into every kick, a drum kit, and a melody struck on tuned steel.
  • Four dead stops inside the drop. The last bar thins to the 808 and the ticking under the brand, then stops hard. -14 LUFS, -1.3 dBTP.

The footage it was cut from

First render the footage: 6-10 shots of an invented watch that read as real footage, with no people and no brands.

What the skill did

  • Nine shots of the VORSA HB-10, modelled, lit and animated in three.js (pinned r160), 3-4 s each, rendered frame-exact at 120 fps with 2 subframes of motion blur.
  • A lens pass on every frame: bokeh depth of field from the depth buffer, bloom, halation, chromatic aberration, ACES tone mapping and grain. A strip light sweeps the studio reflections.
  • The watch's own mechanics drive the shots: a 10 Hz seconds hand that stops when the crown is pulled, a bezel clicking once a beat, a swinging rotor and a 5 Hz balance wheel, and lume taking over as the lights go down.
  • Shown here at real speed, 1.1 s of each shot, ungraded and silent.
